whatIs.title: What is COMPASS?
whatIs.intro: The Complementarity Assessment (COMPASS) framework is a transparent, points-based system that evaluates EP applications. It ensures that EP holders complement Singapore's workforce by assessing both individual attributes (salary, qualifications) and firm-related attributes (diversity, local employment support).

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Everything you need to know about qualification verification for COMPASS.

items.question: What is COMPASS and how does it affect my EP application?
items.answer: COMPASS (Complementarity Assessment Framework) is a points-based framework by Singapore's Ministry of Manpower for evaluating Employment Pass applications. From 1 September 2023, all new EP applications must pass COMPASS with at least 40 points across four foundational criteria. This applies to new applications from September 2023, and renewals from September 2024. Qualification verification under criterion C2 is mandatory.

items.question: What is the two-stage EP eligibility framework?
items.answer: MOM requires EP candidates to pass two stages: Stage 1 — meet the qualifying salary for their sector. Stage 2 — pass the COMPASS framework with at least 40 points across criteria covering salary, qualifications, diversity, and local employment support. Post-secondary qualifications declared must be supported with verification proof.

items.question: Why do I need primary source verification?
items.answer: MOM requires that all educational qualifications (post-secondary diploma and above) declared in work pass applications be verified through an independent background screening company. Primary source verification involves directly contacting the issuing institution to confirm the authenticity of your qualification. Educational certificates certified by notary public and school letters are NOT accepted as verification proof.

items.question: When is an accreditation check required?
items.answer: If your awarding institution is found in MOM's dropdown list, only an authenticity check (education verification) is needed. If the institution is NOT in MOM's dropdown list, you must carry an authenticity check and an accreditation check to confirm the institution is recognized by the country's local government authorities.

items.question: Which work pass types require verification?
items.answer: Verification is required for Employment Pass (EP), S Pass, Training Employment Pass (TEP), ONE Pass, and Personalized Employment Pass (PEP) applications where educational qualifications are declared to MOM.

items.question: How long does the verification process take?
items.answer: Standard verification takes 10–15 working days depending on the institution's response time. Express service is available at SGD 54 + 9% GST (SGD 58.86), reducing turnaround to ≤ 7 working days.

items.question: How much does verification cost?
items.answer: Education verification costs SGD 99 + 9% GST (SGD 108) per qualification. Accreditation check is SGD 30 + 9% GST (SGD 33) per check (optional, only if institution is not in MOM's list). Express service is SGD 54 + 9% GST (SGD 58.86) per application. Some universities may charge an additional verification fee which will be converted to SGD.

items.question: How many qualifications can I verify in one application?
items.answer: You can verify up to 7 educational qualifications in a single application. Each qualification is charged separately at SGD 99 + GST. Accreditation checks are optional and charged at SGD 30 + GST per check.

items.question: What documents do I need to submit?
items.answer: You'll need: (1) Valid passport for identity verification; (2) Degree certificate or diploma; (3) Marksheets or grade sheets; (4) Official transcripts. For non-English documents, the original document and an authorized English translation. All documents must be uploaded digitally. You'll also need the address, contact, and person details of your awarding institution.

items.question: What if my name on the passport differs from my degree?
items.answer: If your name on the passport differs from that on your educational documents, please upload an explanation letter and supporting documents (e.g., deed poll, marriage certificate, or name change certificate or affidavit) during the application process.

items.question: Do some universities charge additional verification fees?
items.answer: Yes, some universities charge their own verification fee. If applicable, we will inform you of the amount during the application. This fee will be converted to SGD and added to your total before payment. Externally charged change processing or transaction surcharges may apply for this fee for non-SGD settlement.

items.question: What payment methods do you accept?
items.answer: We accept all major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express). Payment is collected at the end of the application process after you review and digitally sign the Letter of Authorization (LOA). All prices are subject to 9% GST.

items.question: Will I receive a tax invoice?
items.answer: Yes, upon payment you will receive a detailed tax invoice showing the breakdown of: education verification charges (SGD 99 + GST per qualification), accreditation charges (SGD 30 + GST if opted), university verification fees (if any), express service charges (SGD 54 + GST if opted), and total GST amount.

items.question: What is the Letter of Authorization (LOA)?
items.answer: The LOA is a legal document authorizing HelloVerify to contact your educational institution to verify your qualifications. It is similar to a Letter of Consent used by other employment agencies. You will digitally sign this document before proceeding with payment.

items.question: Can my employer submit the verification on my behalf?
items.answer: Both candidates and employers or agencies can submit verification requests. Candidates can use our self-service portal, while employers can contact our sales team for bulk verification requests and dedicated account support.

items.question: What's included in the verification report?
items.answer: Your verification report includes a summary, identity details, authenticity status, each qualification, accreditation status for each institution (if applicable), direct confirmation from issuing institutions, and a forgery-protected, MOM-compliant report ready for work pass submission.

items.question: What happens after verification is complete?
items.answer: Once verification is complete, you will receive a final verification report that can be submitted as part of your work pass application to MOM. The report confirms the authenticity (and accreditation, if opted) of your educational qualifications.

items.question: What if my qualification cannot be verified?
items.answer: If an institution is unresponsive or unable to verify, we will provide a detailed report explaining the verification attempt and outcome. In some cases, alternative verification methods may be explored. We make unlimited attempts to contact the institution.

items.question: Is HelloVerify an MOM-empaneled vendor?
items.answer: Yes, HelloVerify is an empaneled background screening company recognized by Singapore's Ministry of Manpower for work pass qualification verification. MOM selects vendors based on customer support capabilities, geographical coverage, cost efficiency, and quality of verification processes.
